TS07 — Advanced architecture demonstrations and performance interpretation¶

Goal¶

Compare five small architecture demonstrations under the same two-track contracts as TS06. Understand what the score measures, whether a more complex architecture helps in this experiment, and how a fixed family differs from a selected procedure. These are adaptations for smoothed-input regression, not reproductions of the published long-horizon benchmark models. Both research tracks receive equal treatment.

Observed results¶

Five compact architecture demonstrations were compared with three seeds each. At five sessions, selected returns MSE skill is 0.0767 against zero across 30 origins. At five sessions, selected smoothed MSE skill is 0.1333 against filter_nochange across 30 origins. Compare the family, seed and frozen-procedure results separately. These previously examined single-asset results do not establish a trading advantage.

Setup¶

Use the same environment as TS06 (CPU PyTorch >=2.5). No new installation, model weights, downloads or earlier notebook execution are needed. Preserve the bundled snapshot and frozen TS04–TS06 procedure references. The snapshot was examined in earlier experiments; this is exploratory comparison rather than an untouched test.

Steps¶

1. Define the architectures and their limits¶

All models map a 20 × 2 history of fast/slow causal EMA changes to five target outputs. Track A predicts future fast-EMA log level via residuals around its unchanged-price catch-up; track B predicts actual cumulative future log returns. A future smoothed target is easier partly because it averages price innovations; its score must not be read as an actual-return forecast score.

Demonstration Implemented mechanism Difference from original literature
DecompositionLinear Width-5 moving-average trend + remainder, separate shared time projections, channel readout Inspired by DLinear; regression targets differ from either input channel; no seasonal interpretation claimed
LastCenteredLinear Subtract latest input, temporal linear map, add latest input, channel readout Inspired by NLinear; operates on EMA changes, not a level being forecast
NBEATS Three generic blocks, each two width-12 hidden layers, residual backcast and summed forecast Flattened two-channel features; no interpretable polynomial/Fourier bases, original stack depth or benchmark ensemble
NHITS Three residual blocks with time pooling 4/2/1 and forecast knots 1/3/5, linear interpolation Small multivariate feature adapter, not the original long-horizon implementation
PatchTransformer Four nonoverlapping length-5 joint-channel patches, learned positions, one encoder, width 12, two heads Patching inspired by PatchTST; not channel-independent PatchTST, no RevIN or pretraining

The decomposition averages only positions inside the already observed input window. Attention sees all historical patches; no decoder or future token is supplied. Within-history bidirectional attention is permissible at the forecast origin. A causal mask would be required for predictions made inside that history, which this demo does not make. All five outputs are direct, with no recursive teacher forcing.

for spec in models:

    catalogue.append({**asdict(spec),'parameter_count':sum(p.numel() for p in network.parameters()),

ax.barh(names,catalogue.parameter_count,color=[colors[n] for n in names])
ax.set(title='Trainable parameters — compact demonstrations',xlabel='Parameter count')
save_figure(fig,OUT,'01_architecture_sizes');

2. Check elementary cases before the stock experiment¶

If the decomposition's trend and remainder projections are identical, their sum reduces algebraically to a single linear projection with two biases. The decomposition alone adds no information. With all model parameters zero, standardized output is zero; inverse target scaling yields the training target mean, not necessarily the operational baseline. This distinction matters when interpreting standardized losses.

We also report calibration fitting errors on a deterministic planted mapping and on independent targets. These are training errors, not prediction evidence. They check finite optimization and output shapes without selecting models or tuning the stock experiment. Limited epochs need not recover even a realizable function.

torch.manual_seed(SEED)
net=LinearAdapter(20,2,True);net.trend.load_state_dict(net.temporal.state_dict())
probe=torch.randn(4,20,2)
expected=net.readout((net.temporal(probe.transpose(1,2))+net.temporal.bias).transpose(1,2)).squeeze(-1)
torch.testing.assert_close(net(probe),expected,atol=3e-7,rtol=1e-6)
rng=np.random.default_rng(SEED)
Xtoy=rng.normal(size=(100,20,2));toy_origins=np.arange(100,200)
planted=np.stack([.4*Xtoy[:,-1,0]-.2*Xtoy[:,-2,1]+h*.03 for h in range(1,6)],axis=1)
toy_rows=[]
for case,ytoy in [('Planted linear map',planted),('Independent targets',rng.normal(size=(100,5)))]:
    for spec in models:
        fitted,detail=fit_neural(Xtoy,ytoy,toy_origins,spec,seed=SEED)
        predicted=np.array([fitted.predict(seq) for seq in Xtoy])
        mse=np.mean((predicted-ytoy)**2);den=np.mean((ytoy-ytoy.mean(axis=0))**2)
        toy_rows.append({'case':case,'model':spec.name,'training_MSE':mse,
                        'training_MSE_skill_vs_mean':1-mse/den,'chosen_epochs':detail['chosen_epochs']})
toy_table=pd.DataFrame(toy_rows);toy_table.to_csv(OUT/'toy_optimization_checks.csv',index=False)
display(toy_table.round(4))
print('PASS: exact linear-decomposition identity; toy results are in-sample diagnostics only.')

3. Hold the training and selection budget fixed¶

Match TS06: 252 mature examples, 20% chronological stopping tail, purge all training labels that reach the first stopping feature origin, maximum 30 epochs, patience 5, AdamW at 0.005, weight decay 0.001, full batch, gradient norm at most 1, CPU and three fixed seeds. Use stopping-training-only scalers; after epoch choice reset the model and refit all mature examples and their scalers. No warm starts or best-seed selection.

For 252 examples the split has 196 optimization, 5 purged and 51 validation rows. Fit all three seeds per architecture/track at every origin. A failed member makes the whole architecture fall back to its declared baseline and remains visible. Choose separately by track from three earlier inner origins per block using equal- horizon relative MAE; freeze that choice for the block. Outer scores use 30 origins spaced 40 observed sessions apart; the latest additional origin is unscored. The last label of every fit is available by the forecast origin.

dataset=SupervisedData(market_x,features)
X,y,origins=dataset.training(999,'returns',settings['max_samples'])
tr,va=chronological_holdout(origins)
assert (len(tr),len(va))==(196,51)
assert origins[tr[-1]]+5<origins[va[0]] and origins[-1]+5<=999
run=nested_learned(market_x,models,mode='neural',feature_spec=features,seeds=seeds,
    checkpoint_dir=OUT/'checkpoints',**settings,progress=True)
scores,uncertainty=export_learning(run,OUT);records=run['forecasts'];audit=run['fit_audit']
display(run['selections'][['block','track','chosen_model','selection_cutoff']])
fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12,4.8))
for ax,track in zip(axes,['smoothed','returns']):
    for name in colors:
        part=scores[(scores.track==track)&(scores.model==name)]
        ax.plot(part.horizon,part.MSE_skill,'o-',ms=3,color=colors[name],label=name.replace('_demo',''))
    ax.axhline(0,color='.5',ls='--',lw=1)
    ax.set(title=f'{track.title()} track — 30 scored origins',xlabel='Horizon (sessions)',ylabel='MSE skill vs track baseline')
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)
save_figure(fig,OUT,'02_outer_architecture_skill');

4. Read performance without mixing targets, metrics or selection¶

MAE averages absolute errors; RMSE emphasizes large misses. Smaller is better. MSE skill is $1-\mathrm{MSE}_{model}/\mathrm{MSE}_{baseline}$ on identical origins. Thus +0.20 means 20% lower MSE, equivalent to $\sqrt{0.8}=0.8944$ times baseline RMSE (10.56% lower RMSE). It does not mean 20% correct predictions or 20% returns. Negative skill means the baseline did better. Report log errors in log basis points ($10^4$ times log error); these are not exact arithmetic-return basis points.

A family score evaluates the same architecture's equal-seed ensemble at every outer origin. The selected procedure can change families or choose the baseline between blocks using past inner data. Its score can be worse than a family noticed afterward. That hindsight family is not a valid substitute for the frozen procedure. Selection admits only these five architecture ensembles plus the track baseline; filter drift and raw drift are reported diagnostics, not selection candidates. A positive score against the null does not imply beating these stronger drift benchmarks. Selection minimizes relative MAE, while training minimizes standardized MSE, so selection need not maximize reported MSE skill. The tiny inner sample makes choices noisy. Compare track A only against its filter-aware unchanged-price baseline and track B only against zero actual return; their skill denominators are different.

interpret=scores[scores.model.isin(['selected_pipeline','filter_nochange','zero']+names)].copy()
interpret['MAE_log_bps']=interpret.MAE*1e4;interpret['RMSE_log_bps']=interpret.RMSE*1e4
interpret['RMSE_ratio_to_baseline']=np.sqrt(1-interpret.MSE_skill)
interpret.to_csv(OUT/'performance_interpretation.csv',index=False)
for track in ['smoothed','returns']:
    display(interpret.query('track==@track and horizon==5')[['model','n','MAE_log_bps','RMSE_log_bps','MAE_skill','MSE_skill']].round(4))
comparison=frozen_comparison(records,{label:REF/f'{label}.csv' for label in ['TS04_selected','TS05_selected','TS06_selected']},
                            REF/'metadata.json','TS07_selected')
comparison.to_csv(OUT/'matched_prior_pipeline_comparison.csv',index=False)

5. Separate seed sensitivity, fit budgets and historical uncertainty¶

Seed dots are initialization sensitivity; hollow diamonds are their ensemble scores. They are not independent market samples or confidence intervals. Epoch counts are chosen using historical stopping loss. The calibration trace below is predeclared: patch transformer, first inner origin, actual-return track, first seed.

Moving-block percentile ranges below concern selected-minus-baseline mean absolute loss at five sessions, not MSE skill or the next forecast. Blocks count scheduled origins, not days. Negative values favor the selected procedure. A range crossing zero does not resolve a difference under that resampling design. Prior exploration, multiple architecture searches, asset selection and nonstationarity are not corrected by these ranges. Forecast-distribution calibration is reserved for TS08.

seed_scores=pd.read_csv(OUT/'seed_scorecards.csv')
fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12,4.7))
for ax,track in zip(axes,['smoothed','returns']):
    for j,name in enumerate(names):
        part=seed_scores.query('track==@track and family==@name and horizon==5')
        ax.scatter(j+np.linspace(-.12,.12,len(part)),part.MSE_skill,color=colors[name])
        ensemble=scores.query('track==@track and model==@name and horizon==5').MSE_skill.iloc[0]
        ax.scatter(j,ensemble,marker='D',s=60,facecolors='none',edgecolors='black')
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(names)),[n.replace('_demo','').replace('Linear','\nLinear').replace('Transformer','\nTransformer') for n in names],fontsize=8)
    ax.axhline(0,color='.5',ls='--')
    ax.set(title=f'{track.title()} — seeds and ensemble',ylabel='Five-session MSE skill')

Checks¶

Verify mature labels, purged stopping timing, frozen choices, complete ensemble averaging and exact inference-checkpoint restoration. Prefix-poisoning tests also verify that changing observations after a forecast origin cannot change its forecast. All saved latest forecasts remain unscored until their target sessions are observed. No outer result chooses architecture sizes, seeds, epochs or smoothing settings.

assert (audit.max_training_label<=audit.origin_pos).all()
valid=seed_audit[seed_audit.fit_status=='ok']
assert (valid.optimization_last_label<valid.validation_first_origin).all()
assert (valid.last_training_label<=valid.origin_pos).all()
assert (run['selections'].inner_last_label<=run['selections'].selection_cutoff).all()
assert records[records.origin==market_x.index[-1]].status.eq('immature').all()
members=run['seed_forecasts'].groupby(['origin','track','horizon','model']).prediction.mean()
for row in records[(records.model.isin(names))&(records.fit_status=='ok')].itertuples():
    assert abs(row.prediction-members.loc[(row.origin,row.track,row.horizon,row.model)])<1e-12
checks=[]
for path in sorted((OUT/'checkpoints').glob('*.pt')):
    state=torch.load(path,map_location='cpu',weights_only=True)
    restored=NeuralFit.restore(state)
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(restored.predict(state['sequence'].numpy()),state['residual_prediction'].numpy())
    checks.append({'checkpoint':path.name,'restored_prediction_equal':True})
pd.DataFrame(checks).to_csv(OUT/'checkpoint_checks.csv',index=False)
assert len(checks)==len(models)*len(seeds)*2
write_advanced_manifest(OUT,{'features':asdict(features),'models':[asdict(m) for m in models],**settings,
    'seeds':list(seeds),'seed_policy':'equal-weight complete ensemble; never best-seed selection',
    'training':'same deterministic CPU full-batch budget as TS06; purged chronological stopping and reset/refit'},
    {'market':metadata,'references':reference_metadata},seed=SEED)
selected=scores.query("model=='selected_pipeline' and horizon==5")
summary='## Observed results'+chr(10)*2+'Five compact architecture demonstrations were compared with three seeds each. '
for row in selected.itertuples():
    summary+=f'At five sessions, selected **{row.track}** MSE skill is **{row.MSE_skill:.4f}** against **{row.baseline}** across **{row.n}** origins. '
summary+='Compare the family, seed and frozen-procedure results separately. These previously examined single-asset results do not establish a trading advantage.'
(OUT/'observed_summary.md').write_text(summary)
print('PASS: mature labels, purged stopping, exact seed averaging and all checkpoint round trips.')

PASS: mature labels, purged stopping, exact seed averaging and all checkpoint round trips.

Next Steps¶

TS08 will address probabilistic forecasts and chronological calibration for both tracks. Longer histories, wider models and tuning, more assets and prospective validation require separately specified experiments. This five-session, 20-input- session comparison does not test the original papers' long-horizon claims.

Primary references: N-BEATS, N-HiTS, DLinear/NLinear, PatchTST. The architecture table specifies what this notebook implements and omits.
